**Sentence 1: Row Space and Nullspace**

The row space of a matrix A is the set of all linear combinations of the rows of A. The nullspace of A is the set of all vectors x such that Ax = 0.

The statement claims that the row space of A is orthogonal to the nullspace. This means that if you take any vector x in the nullspace and project it onto any row of A, the result will be 0.

To see why this is true, consider the equation Ax = 0. This equation says that the dot product of x with each row of A is 0. In other words, if you take the dot product of x with the i-th row of A, denoted as r_i, then r_i · x = 0.

Now, suppose we take a linear combination of the rows of A, say a_1r_1 + a_2r_2 +... + a_nr_n. If we project this linear combination onto x, we get:

(a_1r_1 + a_2r_2 +... + a_nr_n) · x = a_1(r_1 · x) + a_2(r_2 · x) +... + a_n(r_n · x) = 0

Since r_i · x = 0 for each i, the entire expression is equal to 0. This shows that the row space of A is orthogonal to the nullspace.

Now, suppose we take the transpose of A, denoted as AT. The row space of AT is the set of all linear combinations of the rows of AT. Since the rows of AT are the columns of A, the row space of AT is the same as the column space of A.

The statement claims that the row space of AT is perpendicular to the nullspace of AT. This means that if you take any vector x in the nullspace of AT and project it onto any row of AT, the result will be 0.

Since the row space of AT is the same as the column space of A, we can project x onto any column of A instead of any row of AT. This shows that the column space of A is orthogonal to the left nullspace of A.
